standard_prerequisites.name: Projective completion of a separated scheme of finite type of dimension at most one
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the initial immersion X -> Xbar that is then normalized.

standard_prerequisites.name: Relative normalization is finite and normal schemes are discrete valuation rings in codimension one
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma morphisms-lemma-relative-normalization-finite (tag 0BXL) and Lemma morphisms-lemma-relative-normalization-normal-codim-1 (tag 0BXN)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first gives finiteness of the normalization and the second identifies the boundary local rings as discrete valuation rings.

core_obligations: Start from the open immersion j : X -> Xbar given by the projective completion lemma (proof lines 9281-9282).

Consider the normalization X' of Xbar in X and use the relative normalization lemma to get that X' -> Xbar is finite, hence projective, hence H-projective over Xbar; compose with the H-projectivity of Xbar over k to obtain H-projectivity of X' over k (proof lines 9283-9291).

Let x'_1, ..., x'_m be the inverse image of the boundary points and observe dim(O_{X', x'_i}) = 1, so that the relative normalization lemma for normal codimension one makes those local rings discrete valuation rings (proof lines 9292-9298).
Conclude that X -> X' together with the set of points x'_i satisfies all four requirements (proof line 9299).
proof_roadmap: Take the projective completion and normalize it in X.
Upgrade finiteness of the normalization to H-projectivity.
Identify the boundary points and their local rings as discrete valuation rings.
Conclude the open immersion has the stated properties.
difficulty_reason: The lemma completes a reduced separated finite type scheme of dimension at most one to an H-projective scheme in such a way that the boundary consists of closed points whose local rings are discrete valuation rings. The proof starts from the projective completion obtained in a previous lemma and takes the normalization X' of the completion in X; the relative normalization lemma makes X' -> X-completion finite, hence projective, hence H-projective over the completion, and by composition H-projective over k (proof lines 9281-9291). The inverse image of the boundary points is then a finite set of points at which X' has one-dimensional local rings, and the relative normalization lemma for normal codimension one shows those local rings are discrete valuation rings, so that X -> X' is the required open immersion (proof lines 9292-9299). H2: the normalization step and the H-projectivity bookkeeping are the substance.
